'''Zhenghan Wang''' ({{lang-zh|王正汉}}; born April 26, 1965)  is a [[Chinese Americans|Chinese-American]] [[mathematician]]. He is a principal researcher at [[Microsoft Station Q]], as well as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].

== Education and career ==
Wang graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] and [[Master of Science|M.S.]] from the [[University of Science and Technology of China]] in 1989 and obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1993 from [[University of California, San Diego|UC San Diego]] under the supervision of [[Michael Freedman]].<ref name="Institute for Optical Science 2021 u823">{{cite web | title=Engineering New Physical Reality: Quantum Computing with Topological Materials | website=Institute for Optical Science | date=12 March 2021 | url=https://opticalscience.osu.edu/events/zhenghan-wang-engineering-new-physical-reality-quantum-computing-topological-materials | access-date=30 March 2024}}</ref> From 1993 to 1996 Wang taught as an assistant professor at the [[University of Michigan]] and from 1996 to 2007 Wang taught at [[Indiana University Bloomington]]. For the majority of this time, Wang specialized in the topology of [[4-manifold]]s.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Lin |first1=Xiao-Song |title=On Ohtsuki's invariants of integral homology 3-spheres, I |date=1996-04-26 |last2=Wang |first2=Zhenghan|arxiv=q-alg/9509009 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Zhenghan |date=1995 |title=Classification of closed nonorientable 4-manifolds with infinite cyclic fundamental group |url=https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/1995/0002/0003/MRL-1995-0002-0003-a011.pdf |journal=Mathematical Research Letters |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=339–344 |doi=10.4310/MRL.1995.v2.n3.a11 |via=intlpress}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Zhenghan |last2=Freedman |first2=Michael |date=1994 |title=CP2-STABLE THEORY |url=https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/1994/0001/0001/MRL-1994-0001-0001-a005.pdf |journal=Mathematical Research Letters |volume=1 |issue=1 |page=4 |via=intlpress}}</ref>

In 2005, Wang moved to Santa Barbara to serve as a lead scientist in the newly founded research institute Microsoft Station Q. At Station Q, Wang worked with Michael Freedman (the station's director and his former Ph.D. advisor) on the foundations of [[topological quantum computing]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zhenghan Wang at Microsoft Research |url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/people/zhenghwa/ |access-date=2024-03-30 |website=Microsoft Research |language=en-US}}</ref> Since 2012 Wang has served as a full professor at [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UC Santa Barbara]].<ref name="Institute for Optical Science 2021 u823"/> From 2013 to 2020 Wang served as a distinguished visiting research chair at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] as well.<ref name="Institute for Optical Science 2021 u823"/> Wang was included in the 2019 class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2019 |access-date=2024-03-30 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==

=== Topological Quantum Computing ===
Zhenghan Wang's most notable contributions are in the field of [[Topological quantum computer|topological quantum computation]]. In a series of early papers with Michael Freedman, [[Michael J. Larsen]], and [[Alexei Kitaev]], Wang established the abstract equivalence of topological quantum computation with the [[Quantum circuit|quantum circuit model]].<ref>{{Citation |last1=Freedman |first1=Michael H. |title=Topological Quantum Computation |date=2002-09-20 |last2=Kitaev |first2=Alexei |last3=Larsen |first3=Michael J. |last4=Wang |first4=Zhenghan|arxiv=quant-ph/0101025 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last1=Freedman |first1=Michael |title=A modular functor which is universal for quantum computation |date=2000-02-01 |last2=Larsen |first2=Michael |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan|arxiv=quant-ph/0001108 |bibcode=2000quant.ph..1108F }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Freedman |first1=Michael H. |last2=Kitaev |first2=Alexei |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan |date=2002-06-01 |title=Simulation of topological field theories by quantum computers |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=227 |issue=3 |pages=587–603 |doi=10.1007/s002200200635 |arxiv=quant-ph/0001071 |bibcode=2002CMaPh.227..587F |issn=0010-3616}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Freedman |first1=Michael H. |last2=Larsen |first2=Michael J. |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan |date=2002-06-01 |title=The two-eigenvalue problem and density of Jones representation of braid groups |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=228 |issue=1 |pages=177–199 |doi=10.1007/s002200200636 |arxiv=math/0103200 |bibcode=2002CMaPh.228..177F |issn=0010-3616}}</ref> The implication of these works for [[topological phase]]s is that the Fibonacci [[Anyon|anyon model]] can be used to make a universal quantum computer, and the implication of these works for quantum circuits is the [[Aharonov–Jones–Landau algorithm]].<ref>{{Citation |last1=Aharonov |first1=Dorit |title=A Polynomial Quantum Algorithm for Approximating the Jones Polynomial |date=2006-04-10 |last2=Jones |first2=Vaughan |last3=Landau |first3=Zeph|arxiv=quant-ph/0511096 }}</ref> Wang has also introduced several other schemes for universal topological quantum computation using [[anyon]]s which are more likely to be experimentally realizable.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cui |first1=Shawn X. |last2=Hong |first2=Seung-Moon |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan |date=August 2015 |title=Universal quantum computation with weakly integral anyons |journal=Quantum Information Processing |volume=14 |issue=8 |pages=2687–2727 |doi=10.1007/s11128-015-1016-y |arxiv=1401.7096 |bibcode=2015QuIP...14.2687C |issn=1570-0755}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Levaillant |first1=Claire SU$(2)_4$ Anyons |journal=Physical Review A |volume=92 |issue=1 |article-number=012301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.92.012301 |arxiv=1504.02098 |issn=1050-2947}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cong |first1=Iris |last2=Cheng |first2=Meng |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan |date=2017-10-25 |title=Universal Quantum Computation with Gapped Boundaries |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=119 |issue=17 |article-number=170504 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.170504 |pmid=29219455 |arxiv=1707.05490 |bibcode=2017PhRvL.119q0504C |issn=0031-9007}}</ref>

=== The Algebraic Theory of Topological Phases ===
Outside of direct applications to topological quantum computing, Wang has made many contributions to the formal algebraic theory of two dimensional [[Topological order|topological quantum phases of matter]]. This includes work on the structure and classification of [[boson]]ic topological order (modular tensor categories),<ref>{{Citation |last1=Rowell |first1=Eric |title=On classification of modular tensor categories |date=2009-11-09 |last2=Stong |first2=Richard |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan|arxiv=0712.1377 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bruillard |first1=Paul |last2=Ng |first2=Siu-Hung === Higher Dimensional Topological Quantum Field Theory ===
In addition to his work on two dimensional [[topological order]], Wang has also worked in the theory of three dimensional [[topological quantum field theory]]. Here he is most well known introducing the Walker-Wang model along with his coauthor Kevin Walker.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walker-Wang model in nLab |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Walker-Wang+model |access-date=2024-03-23 |website=ncatlab.org}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last1=Walker |first1=Kevin |title=(3+1)-TQFTs and Topological Insulators |date=2011-04-27 |last2=Wang |first2=Zhenghan|arxiv=1104.2632 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Williamson |first1=Dominic J. |last2=Wang |first2=Zhenghan |date=February 2017 |title=Hamiltonian models for topological phases of matter in three spatial dimensions |journal=Annals of Physics |volume=377 |pages=311–344 |doi=10.1016/j.aop.2016.12.018 |arxiv=1606.07144 |bibcode=2017AnPhy.377..311W |issn=0003-4916}}</ref> This theory has been used to describe the boundaries of [[topological insulator]]s<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Burnell |first1=F. J. |author1-link=Fiona Burnell|last2=Chen |first2=Xie |last3=Fidkowski |first3=Lukasz |last4=Vishwanath |first4=Ashvin |date=2014-12-15 |title=Exactly Soluble Model of a 3D Symmetry Protected Topological Phase of Bosons with Surface Topological Order |journal=Physical Review B |volume=90 |issue=24 |article-number=245122 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.90.245122 |arxiv=1302.7072 |issn=1098-0121}}</ref> and to construct nontrivial [[Quantum cellular automaton|quantum cellular automata]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haah |first1=Jeongwan |last2=Fidkowski |first2=Lukasz |last3=Hastings |first3=Matthew B. |date=February 2023 |title=Nontrivial Quantum Cellular Automata in Higher Dimensions |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=398 |issue=1 |pages=469–540 |doi=10.1007/s00220-022-04528-1 |arxiv=1812.01625 |bibcode=2023CMaPh.398..469H |issn=0010-3616}}</ref> Wang has also made contributions to the theory of three dimensional [[Fracton (subdimensional particle)|fracton phases]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shirley |first1=Wilbur |last2=Slagle |first2=Kevin |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan |last4=Chen |first4=Xie |date=2018-08-29 |title=Fracton Models on General Three-Dimensional Manifolds |journal=Physical Review X |volume=8 |issue=3 |article-number=031051 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.8.031051 |arxiv=1712.05892 |bibcode=2018PhRvX...8c1051S |issn=2160-3308}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last1=Tian |first1=Kevin T. |title=Generalized Haah Codes and Fracton Models |date=2019-10-12 |arxiv=1902.04543 |last2=Wang |first2=Zhenghan}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Wang has been married to Dr. Yanyun Chen since 1993. They have two children, a daughter and a son.
